exposure: 'top-up' of labour epidural analgesia (tEDA) with local anaesthesia and fentanyl mixture
cohort: 135 women who underwent emergency caesarean section (ECS) at Danderyds Hospital, Sweden, between January and October 2016
finding: While general anaesthesia shortened the DDI for ECS, both spinal anaesthesia and 'top-up' epidural analgesia with opioid supplementation maintained a short DDI and should be considered when time allows.
mod_finding: GA shortened the DDI for ECS compared to SPA and tEDA, but Apgar <7 at 5' was more common in the GA group.
